sections.html:
Elkhart County sits in northern Indiana on the Michigan line. Goshen is the county seat and Elkhart is the largest city, with Middlebury, Nappanee, Bristol and Wakarusa rounding out the incorporated places. The 2020 census counted 207,047 people, and the 2025 estimate is 208,774.

Two rivers shape where houses sit. The St. Joseph River is the main waterway, and the Elkhart River runs through Goshen and Dunlap before joining it in the city of Elkhart. A house near either river or on Simonton Lake brings drainage and insurance questions that a farm parcel near Nappanee does not.

Elkhart County calls itself the RV Capital of the World, and the recreational vehicle business drives local household budgets. When plants cut hours, a property tax installment is often one of the first bills to slip. That is how many owners here end up selling with taxes due.

The swings can be sharp. Manufacturing, which covers RV makers and their suppliers, held 49.6% of county jobs in April 2006, fell to 38.4% by April 2009, and climbed back to 46% by April 2016. Unemployment peaked at 18.9% in March 2009 and stood at 3.9% in April 2016. Those are decade-old figures, so read them as a pattern and not a current number. The pattern is why buyers and lenders here pay close attention to how long a house has sat and whether the taxes are current.

Indiana splits the work among several county offices. The assessor sets values and hears appeals. The auditor applies tax cap credits to each bill. The treasurer mails bills and collects payment. Rates come from the local taxing units on your parcel, such as the county, a city or town, and a school corporation.

Circuit breaker caps limit your bill as a share of gross assessed value. They do not change the local rate. Whatever the rate would produce above the cap, the auditor credits back.

Property classCap on tax as share of gross assessed value
Homestead1%
Other residential, including rentals2%
Agricultural land2%
Nonresidential and personal property3%

The 1% cap requires the homestead standard deduction. A homestead covers the dwelling, a garage and up to one acre of surrounding land. Many rural lots here run larger than an acre, and the extra land falls into the 2% class. The state posts each county's budget order every January, and Elkhart County's 2026 order was issued January 15, 2026.

The county reviews roughly a quarter of its parcels each year, so a different set of townships gets a fresh look every cycle. In the 2024 phase, Baugo, Benton and Cleveland townships had residential and agricultural property reviewed, Concord had most districts reviewed in all classes, and York had commercial and exempt parcels reviewed.

The ratio study that tests those values used sales from January 1 to December 31, 2024, and handled improved residential property one township at a time because each had enough sales. A land order sent to the county board on December 3, 2024 took effect January 1, 2025.

  • Every sales disclosure form is checked through phone contacts, aerial maps, field visits, MLS records and CoStar.
  • Permits for all trades go into the county's assessment system. Elkhart, Goshen and Nappanee process their own permits, and the county handles the rest.

The practical point for a seller: a recent remodel or addition that was permitted will show up in the assessment, so check the property record card before you list and fix errors early.

File a Form 130 with the county assessor, one form per parcel. The deadline is June 15. Which June 15 depends on when the Form 11 assessment notice was mailed. If it went out before May 1, the deadline falls in that assessment year. If it was mailed on or after May 1, the deadline falls in the year the tax bill is mailed. If no notice was sent, the tax bill counts as the notice.

After you file, the assessor schedules an informal meeting to compare information. The county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals must then hold a hearing within 180 days of your filing, with at least 30 days of written notice to you. A continuance request needs good cause and must be filed at least 10 days ahead. Skipping the hearing without a request can bring a $50 penalty.

If you disagree with the result, or the board does not act within 180 days, file Form 131 with the Indiana Board of Tax Review. Further review goes to the Indiana Tax Court and then the Indiana Supreme Court. While an appeal is pending you may pay on the prior year's assessment without penalty. If you pay less than that amount, the unpaid part is delinquent. The state's appeals fact sheet lays out each step.

Unpaid property tax does not stop a sale. The title company will want it settled at closing, normally out of your proceeds.

Waiting costs more. Under Indiana Code 6-1.1-37-10, a late payment draws a 5% penalty if it comes within 30 days of the due date and the parcel has no earlier delinquency. Otherwise the penalty is 10%. A further 10% of the unpaid principal is added the day after each later installment date. That extra 10% applies only to the tax itself, so it does not compound on earlier penalties. Payments go first to the tax and then to penalties.

  • Ask the treasurer for a current payoff before you list or accept an offer.
  • Ask the title company whether the spring and fall installments are both in the payoff.
  • File the sales disclosure form Indiana requires with the county. A 2021 state memo said a sale closing by December 31 can qualify the buyer for a homestead deduction the next year, and the disclosure form can serve as the application. Confirm the current dates with the auditor.

A cash buyer who does not need a lender can close on a short timeline and take the house as it stands, which skips repairs and showings. The back tax and penalties still come out of the proceeds, so get the number first.

Northern Indiana weather is hard on roofs and basements. Goshen's averages run from a January low near 17 degrees to a July high near 85, and snowfall in the city of Elkhart averages about 74 inches a year.

Flooding has a record here. In February 2018 the Elkhart River in Goshen rose to a record 13.2 feet after heavy rain and snowmelt. More than 300 structures were damaged and some residents had to evacuate. If you have repaired water or storm damage, keep the receipts and permits. Buyers and inspectors ask about basement and drainage history on almost every house near the water.

Buyers here often name the school corporation before the street. Elkhart Community Schools serves most of the city of Elkhart. Concord Community Schools covers the southeast side of Elkhart and northwest Goshen, and Baugo Community Schools covers the southwest side. Goshen Community Schools serves most of Goshen, with small parts covered by Middlebury, Concord and WaNee.

The Indiana Toll Road runs along the northern edge, with exits at Elkhart, Bristol and Middlebury. U.S. 20 follows the southern edge of Elkhart as the St. Joseph Valley Parkway, and U.S. 6, 33 and 131 also cross the county. Goshen's historic district, listed on the National Register in 1983, centers on the county courthouse, and older houses there may come with extra buyer questions about upkeep.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: Start with the county treasurer for bills and payments and the county assessor for values and appeals. The treasurer's office is in the county building in Goshen. The state information center at 1-800-457-8283 also takes general property tax questions.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: The deadline is June 15, filed on Form 130 with the county assessor. Which year it falls in depends on whether the Form 11 notice was mailed before or after May 1. File a separate petition for each parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Elkhart County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the unpaid tax and penalties from your proceeds at closing, so the amount comes off what you receive. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer first.

faqs.q: Why did my Elkhart County bill change when my value went up?
faqs.a: Circuit breaker caps limit the bill to 1% of gross assessed value for a homestead, 2% for other residential and farmland, and 3% for nonresidential property. Without the homestead deduction you do not get the 1% cap.

faqs.q: Does a flood or storm repair affect the sale of a house in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: It can. Buyers and inspectors look at past water damage, so keep receipts and permits. The Elkhart River reached a record 13.2 feet in February 2018, and drainage and basement history comes up in most inspections.
